newsitem.title: USA: US pork group says no misuse of check-off funds.
newsitem.headline: US pork group says no misuse of check-off funds.

text.p: The National Pork Producers Council said Friday that it was within bounds in using check-off funds to monitor "environmental, animal rights, industry structure and food safety issues."
"They are issues that are likely to have an impact on the way pork producers do business in the future," NPPC said in a statement.
Earlier, the Agriculture Department said it and NPPC were reviewing several 1996 reports on those topics to see if they were an appropriate use of check-off funds.
NPPC president Jerry King, an Illinois farmer, said the expenditures were acceptable as spending on research.

"We have always operated within what we believed to be the parameters of the Pork Act as established by Congress in 1985 and the best interests of pork producers, and we will continue to do so," King said.
